<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**78** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8fec212c9e593f47af96ba5625c7e51aab992007` — the merge of head `6a1892ec03261c4f9aef1330bb2615d21a54c197` into base `24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8fec212c9e593f47af96ba5625c7e51aab992007 && git checkout 8fec212c9e593f47af96ba5625c7e51aab992007
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821 6a1892ec03261c4f9aef1330bb2615d21a54c197 && git checkout -B drift-repro 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821 && git merge --no-ff 6a1892ec03261c4f9aef1330bb2615d21a54c197

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:spec#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzzqHZdAVqgBAvxXKB

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a1892ec03261c4f9aef1330bb2615d21a54c197`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json, .changeset/seed-landed-keys-31021.md (read for ②); read in the live tree on `main`: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-lifecycle-health.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-secrets-and-routing.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts, and at the head packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts (the `sys_seed_landed_key` read and write paths only). The rest of the diff (loader, AppPlugin, their tests) is the server lane's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #31021 body and its 4 comments (triage 6692929632, claim 6701308503 with the amended file surface, os-dev-reports 6702346336 and 6702739093); PR #31083 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...6a1892ec` (merge base cb8f5200, 13 files, +1062 / -14); the check-runs on the head, read once.

Check-runs on `6a1892ec` (read once, 2026-11-07): every run completed, none pending, none failed. Push run 42339632913: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and the Test Core roll-up success (the spec roster test and the cli inventory test run there), Build Core, Type Check UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate success. Run 42339632867: Lint and Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · scoped (tooling self-tests, query-options erasure, slot lookup and corpus), Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, TypeScript Type Check success. PR-automation: Check Changeset success (twice, run 42339632854 and the later `edited` run 42342476182), PR-body guards success (twice), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label success. Skipped by their own triggers: Build Docs, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Lint UI, Schedule gate.

### ① Derived judgments

The one `hits` hunk adds `'sys_seed_landed_key'` to `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']`, between `sys_secret` and `sys_session`. What that line entails, each judged against the live code:

- **The roster's own contract — RIGHT.** The file header says a group is "the exact set that package registers", and the ratchet `platform-object-names.test.ts` scans every `packages/**/*.object.ts` for its `ObjectSchema.create({ name })` and asserts equality per owning package, both ways. At the head `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts` declares `name: 'sys_seed_landed_key'`, `system/index.ts` exports `SysSeedLandedKey`, and `PlatformObjectsPlugin.init` lists it in the platform-objects manifest `objects: [..., SysRecycleBin, SysSeedLandedKey]`; `plugin.test.ts` pins the registration list and the object's shape. So the name is a real registered platform object, in the right group, in sorted position (the test sorts both sides, so position is tidiness, and it is tidy). The dev measured the ratchet red (1 failed, naming `sys_seed_landed_key`) before the line and 14 passed after it; CI Test Core confirms the after.
- **`PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` follow — RIGHT, a widening.** Accept sets that move, none of which refuses anything it accepted before:
  - `@objectstack/lint` `validate-object-references` rung ③ (and the dataset, nav-target, nav-access, translation and email-template-hole rules that share the ladder): a stack reference to `sys_seed_landed_key` now resolves instead of drawing the `OBJECT_REFERENCE_UNREGISTERED_PLATFORM` advisory.
  - `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` :5395: a top-level action whose `objectName` is `sys_seed_landed_key` is accepted at parse as a known platform object (the engine attaches it when the object is served; a target no loaded package registers is refused at boot, and this one is registered).
  - `ui/packages/data-objectstack` `missingResources`: a 404 on the name is swallowed into an empty result rather than rethrown; consistent with the object's `apiEnabled: false`, and the same treatment `sys_lifecycle_state` and `sys_recycle_bin` get.
  - `@objectstack/objectql` `resolvePrimaryDatasource` (#13408 criterion): the object now votes. It is registered, carries no `lifecycle` block so `isSystemLedgerObject` (lifecycle class in `SYSTEM_LEDGER_LIFECYCLE_CLASSES`) answers false, and it rides the platform-objects manifest whose `defaultDatasource` is undefined (pinned by `plugin.test.ts`: "the eight above must NOT acquire the ledger's routing triple"), so it lands on the datasource the other seven witnesses name. One more witness; no `system-objects-split`.
  - `dangling-reference-audit` `SECURITY_SURFACE_OBJECTS` derives from the `plugin-security` group alone: unaffected. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` :1781 pins `sys_metadata_activation` once in the roster file: unaffected.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec` — unchanged.** No new export; `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` record `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE (const)` as a symbol, not its value, so no regenerated spec artifact is owed (Lint and Repo Gates green on the head agrees).
- **Readers that hold a row per roster name, in the same commit — RIGHT:**
  - `packages/cli` `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY`: its test enumerates `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` ("a platform object without a row reds here, by name"), so the roster line forces the row, and `os migrate organization-ownership` would refuse the table without it. The row `{ object: 'sys_seed_landed_key', census: PMAIN, fate: 'attribution', citation: CENSUS_MAIN (in reach, added since the first census); D10_SINGLE, anchors: [] }` is the `sys_recycle_bin` shape, and it is the right fate: the object carries an authored `organization_id` lookup with tenancy on (the regenerated census reads `reach: in`, `tenantField: organization_id`, `reasons: []`), so `sys_lifecycle_state`'s `column-drop` (ADR-0131 D7, tenant-less) does not apply; the loader stamps every row with the organization the load seeds and keeps no record when it seeds none (`openLandedKeyLedger` returns undefined and says so at `info`), so a NULL row has no producer; a key names its seed row by natural key, not by id, so no parent row anchors it. The test's shape rule "fate 3 names its anchors" is met by `anchors: []`; 26 passed per the dev, Test Core green.
  - `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`: the census script scans `packages/**/*.object.ts` and does not read the roster, so the roster line makes no claim about it; the regeneration is forced by the object, not the line. Totals 96 to 97 registered, 49 to 50 in reach, 47 outside, `reasonTotals` unchanged; `check:platform-object-tenancy-census` exit 0 per the dev's gate run and the repo-gates job.
  - `plugin-audit` `SKIP_OBJECTS` (`AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` is spread from it): not a roster reader; forced by the object being engine-owned bookkeeping written once per landed key. Right on the `sys_lifecycle_state` and `sys_recycle_bin` precedent; the seeded rows themselves stay audited. Not pinned by name in `audit-writers.test.ts` (the dev says so); see ④ should-fix.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/seed-landed-keys-31021.md` grades all six packages the diff moves `src/**` of at `minor` (metadata-protocol, runtime, platform-objects, spec, cli, plugin-audit) and carries both declaration lines at line start, `yes (widening)` on the clause line and `semantic` on the metadata-protocol line; the PR body carries the same two lines. `skip-changeset` is not in play.
- As `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads them: value `yes`, arm `widening`, kind `semantic`. A well-formed pair: the two refused contradictions are `added` under `no` and `narrowed` without the `(narrowing)` arm, and neither is here; `no (widening)` is not here.
- As `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads them (ruling A, 2026-10-21): the level follows the kind alone. `semantic` is the "enforce" lane: at least one package whose published source the diff moves must be graded `minor` or above, and every entry is. A `minor` on spec, cli or plugin-audit is not refused: the gate refuses `none` beside a `minor`, and `patch` on a moved package under a declared kind; it never refuses a `minor` under a kind (its own battery: "the kind asks for the grade, it does not refuse the PR"). No `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head, twice.
- Is `semantic` the right kind for this PR? AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: a changed meaning or default of what a metadata author writes is `semantic`; "several ⇒ `narrowed` over `semantic` over `added`". The replay meaning of the authorable `SeedSchema.mode` values `ignore` and `upsert` changes on AppPlugin's loads (a missing keyed row whose key landed in the organization is no longer inserted). The roster line alone is `added` (#30751 and #30780 declared exactly that for the same one-line shape). Several, so `semantic` outranks `added`. Right.
- Is `yes (widening)` right for the spec face? Yes: ① names the accept sets the line widens (lint rung ③, the stack action target), and nothing is narrowed anywhere under `packages/spec`, so no `(narrowing)` arm and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. For the spec package the level is `minor`, as the two precedents graded it and as the gate reads it. Right.
- One spec-side residual, outside my `hits` and outside the amended surface (the claim forbids any other `packages/spec/**` path): the spec's own published description of `mode` in `packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts` (:176-205 and the `.describe()` text, "a missing row is inserted and an existing row is left as it is") still states the unconditional create-only rule, so the meaning the `semantic` declaration announces is published nowhere in the spec. The PR already owes `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` as follow-up #31090; the `seed.zod.ts` docstring belongs in the same follow-up. Should-fix, carried below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Clause and kind corrected in review** (dev deviation, round 0 and the claim's correction): `yes (widening)` and `semantic`, from the claim's `yes` and `semantic` — answered in ②: right.
- **spec, cli and plugin-audit at `minor`, not `patch`** (dev deviation, round 1): answered in ②: right under ruling A and the #30751 / #30780 changesets.
- **"Nothing else under `packages/spec/**`"** (claim 6701308503, the amended surface): held. `git grep` at the head finds the name under `packages/spec` on the roster line only; the spec diff is that one line.
- **The three forced lines landed by option A** (round 0 `open_questions`, one entry): the seat amended the file surface on the claim and asked this review; the lines are in the same commit as the object, as the `sys_lifecycle_state` precedent and the ratchet require. Answered. Round 1 lists no open question.
- **No named pin for the audit skip** (dev deviation, round 1): the skip is enforced by set membership and `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` is spread from the set; the three audit suites pass with the entry. A pin by name is the `sys_lifecycle_state` shape; should-fix for the server lane, not a roster matter.
- **Docs follow-up #31090** (`Skills-docs:` line): owed and named; add the `seed.zod.ts` `mode` docstring to it (②).
- **Hosted `ArtifactKernelFactory` call site NOT MEASURED** (dev, no cloud read access): a cloud carrier (cloud#3657 item 2), outside the spec face; escalated by the dev, nothing for this record to answer.
- **The seed doors that do not pass `landedKeys` still re-insert a removed row** (dev out-of-scope finding): not a spec matter; the roster line is indifferent to which loads honour the record.
- **ADR check (Prime Directive 13):** no ADR fixes the create-only replay rule; it is ruling 6631016988 on #30081, recorded in `seed.zod.ts`, whose point (a replay must not write the shipped value back over a customer's edit) this diff strengthens rather than reverses. ADR-0131: the object is organization-owned with every row stamped by the load's organization, so D7 (deployment-level state, no organization column) does not apply and the D10 fate is 3, not 1; the inventory row says the same. No ADR amendment owed.
- **No security finding** on the spec face; the object has no data API, is engine-owned and read-gated by `manage_platform_settings`, a capability the spec already names (`eval-user.zod.ts`).

### ④ Design judgment

`hits` file: `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`, one line. Judged against the code it cites (the object, its export, its registration) and the scenarios the roster is accepted against (a stack or tool referencing the name; the primary-datasource verdict; the inventory and census enumerations). Each holds (①). Attempts to break it:

1. *Is the name a cloud-provided or fixture object the roster should not carry?* No: declared under `packages/platform-objects/src/`, a package with no `objectstack.manifest.json` listing, under the `sys_` prefix; the ratchet's "every registered name carries a reserved platform prefix" and "cloud-only names are not declared here" both hold.
2. *Could the new voter split the primary-datasource verdict?* No: same manifest as the other seven, `defaultDatasource` undefined and pinned, no `lifecycle` block so not a §3.6 ledger. One more witness on the same datasource.
3. *Could the roster line make the ownership ceremony refuse the table?* No: the inventory row lands in the same commit and the enumeration pin passes.
4. *Does the object's claim "Deleting an organization deletes its rows" (object header, changeset) hold for an engine-owned object?* `outlivesOrganization` exempts engine-owned objects from the organization-delete refusal and from `set_null` clearing only; the cascade walk (`engine-cascade-planning.ts` :862-882) keeps an authored `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` on its own meaning, which is the mechanism `sys_recycle_bin` relies on under the same `managedBy`. Holds. `plugin.test.ts` pins the declaration, not a cascade run.
5. *Does the roster now let an author seed the record itself?* A dataset over `sys_seed_landed_key` would resolve at lint rung ③, exactly as one over `sys_lifecycle_state` or `sys_recycle_bin` does today; the roster answers "is this name real", not "is it authorable", by design, and the object is engine-owned with no data API. No change asked.
6. *Is a spec-side name constant owed, as `RECYCLE_BIN_OBJECT` is?* No: that constant exists because the spec publishes the recycle-bin entry schema; here the spec publishes nothing about the row, and the `sys_lifecycle_state` precedent spells the name in its writer the same way the loader does. The roster line and `plugin.test.ts` pin the spelling.

Findings:

- **Must-fix:** none.
- **Should-fix S1** (spec, follow-up #31090): amend the `mode` docstring and `.describe()` in `packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts` so the published meaning of `ignore` / `upsert` on replay names the record (a removed row whose key landed in the organization is not inserted again by AppPlugin's loads; the deliberate re-seed is the `seed-replayer` service with `{ reseed: true }`), beside the `content/docs` change the PR already owes.
- **Should-fix S2** (server lane): one case in `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.test.ts` pinning the `sys_seed_landed_key` skip by name, beside the `sys_lifecycle_state` one.
- **Should-fix S3** (server lane, optional): a pin that an organization delete cascades into `sys_seed_landed_key` rows, since the object header and the changeset state it and today only the declaration is pinned.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-31021-seed-landed-keys`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzzqHZdAVqgBAvxXKB`

**VERDICT: PASS**

domain:server#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcTJTE7kSbcMoJQ4Txf

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · Head-sha `6a1892ec03261c4f9aef1330bb2615d21a54c197` · read at 2026-11-07T05:35Z

- **Shape.** Draft into `main`. The body opens `Fixes #31021`, then `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` and `Skills-docs: follow-up #31090`. The changeset carries the clause and kind lines and grades six packages `minor`. 13 files, +1062/−14, all inside the claim's file surface as amended in 6701308503 (the loader and its test, `AppPlugin` and its test, the new `sys_seed_landed_key` object and registration, the regenerated tenancy census, the spec roster line, the CLI inventory row, plugin-audit's `SKIP_OBJECTS` entry, one changeset).
- **Premise measured.** On `origin/main` before dispatch, no landed-key record existed in the loader or runtime. The dev measured that no existing store fits (`sys_setting`, `sys_migration`, `sys_lifecycle_state`, `sys_recycle_bin`), hence the new object.
- **Gate check-runs on this head.** 55 success and 9 skipped, none failed or pending, including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and Test Core, where the spec roster and CLI inventory pins run. `mergeable_state` is `clean`. `check-governed-merges --pr 31083`: NOT governed, 1076 lines ≤ 3000. Generated path `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`: `origin/main` has not touched it (or any other file of this PR) since the merge base `cb8f5200`, so no regeneration is owed.
- **Contract review.** The `domain:spec#1` record 6702871453 is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, PASS, on this head, with no must-fix. This lane seat's `TIER_DEFAULT` read of the remainder:
  - The loader skips a missing keyed row only when its key is recorded as landed in this organization and the row is gone (`existingRecords` does not hold it), so a row an upgrade adds still lands.
  - `reseed` turns off only the honouring, not the recording.
  - Records are written with `isSystem` and an explicit `organization_id`.
  - A write failure is one loud `error` per load, not silent.
  - A load with no organization or no registered object says so at `info` / `warn` and keeps no record.
  - `AppPlugin`'s three loads pass `honour`; the replayer passes `reseed` on `{ reseed: true }`.
  - Ablations A1–A6 cover each branch (dev report 6702346336).
- **Accepted deviations.**
  - spec, cli and plugin-audit are graded `minor` (the spec record judged it right).
  - The CLI inventory fate is `attribution`, not `column-drop`, because the table is organization-scoped.
  - The dev left the PR assignee and the body to the seat; the seat patched the body (`Skills-docs: follow-up #31090`).
  - S2 (pin the audit skip by name) and S3 (pin the organization-delete cascade) are accepted as not done here: both pin behaviour that the set membership and the `deleteBehavior` declaration already give, and the spec record rates them should-fix, with S3 optional.
- **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
  - #31090 carries `seed-data.mdx` and the stale `skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md` mode table; S1 (the `seed.zod.ts` `mode` docstring, spec lane) is added there in a comment.
